contract: Signed outbound events to tenant endpoints over a consumer-owned Ecto Repo on PostgreSQL 19 under the state/tenant-isolation floor (Wave 9 Q5 A): Migration.install/1 creates four protected tables (endpoints, events, deliveries with a dead_letter none/pending/filed mark and the record inputs, observations keyed (tenant, delivery_id, try, attempt)); register/3 egress-checks the https URL with EgressPolicy.resolve/3 under the tenant's policy and is idempotent by endpoint_id; enqueue/3 stores a canonical JSON payload of at most 65,536 bytes once and one delivery per listening endpoint at try 1; claim_due/3 leases due rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and returns each try's delivery/effect-intent admission (identity [tenant, provider_account, webhook-out, post, <delivery_id>/try/<n>], arguments without the payload, deadline fixed at the try's first claim) and a rearm flag; the Adapter reads the rows, resolves the URL again, resolves a whsec_ secret, signs the Standard Webhooks webhook-id/-timestamp/-signature (v1 HMAC-SHA-256 over id.timestamp.body), makes exactly one POST stopped at send_timeout_ms and stores the typed result; record/3 applies one result once per (try, attempt) under the row lock, with a host fallback (delivered, unknown, not_sent, expired): a not-sent refusal is due again on the same try after RetryTimeout.delay/4, a possibly sent failure gets a new try with the same webhook-id only for a dedup endpoint below max_tries, else a dead letter dispatched_unresolved or retries_exhausted, another 4xx or a 3xx is permanent, an expired try is deadline_before_dispatch or deadline_expired; the dead letter is marked pending in the committing transaction and put to delivery/dead-letter-store after it, with file_dead_letters/3 for a put that did not complete. Shape, then the caller's open transaction, are refused before any query; read committed is checked; fixed error atoms that never echo a URL, payload or secret.
limits: The state/tenant-isolation limits apply; the consumer Repo's query telemetry receives every parameter, including payloads, URLs and Secrets references.
READ COMMITTED, the trusted clock, the transport Need's address pinning, the tenant policy and the host's fallback reading of an intent with no observation are host Needs.

Req 0.7.5 with connect_options: [hostname: h] starts one Finch instance per distinct hostname and never stops it; endpoint hosts are tenant-supplied, so the host's transport Need must pool or bound its connections itself.

A delivered event is delivered at least once to a dedup endpoint and at most once to another; a receiver that does not deduplicate by webhook-id may see one event twice only if it was registered as deduplicating.
A webhook-id (the tenant's event_id) is unique only within one tenant: a receiver that serves several tenants scopes its deduplication by endpoint or secret.
Event payloads are kept with no expiry or purge in this version; a timestamp is the sender's clock.
No live receiver is exercised: the evidence is a local receiver through the Req transport behind a resolver double, with no successful public connect.
No endpoint disable, secret rotation, event filters, fan-out bound or asymmetric signature (v1a).
Finite listed scenarios on one local PostgreSQL 19 with volatile effect-intent Memory Stores; not proofs of isolation, atomicity, ordering or delivery.

grounding.claim: Listed scenarios on the worker's own disposable PostgreSQL 19 database behind a fail-closed target guard, DBConnection.ConnectionPool Repos (not the Sandbox), a random schema dropped afterwards, application connections SET ROLE to ELZOO_TEST_APP_ROLE with only the README grants (fails when unset), effect-intent owners on an acknowledged volatile Memory Store, the receiver a Req.Test function plug through the transport Need behind a resolver double: 1 a signed delivery verified by a Standard Webhooks check written from the specification, refused with another secret; 2 a private address refused at register/3 with nothing written, a rebinding name refused at send as not sent with no request; 3 a dropped connection after enqueue/3 leaves both deliveries due; 4 a committed lease hides the row, after it equal admission parts, the recovered owner is read-only and sends nothing, fallback unknown applies the possibly sent rule, and two concurrent claims (one held inside its transaction) take disjoint rows; 5 dedup 503 then 200 gives two tries, two intents, one webhook-id and body, non-dedup 503 one try dead-lettered dispatched_unresolved in delivery/dead-letter-store; 6 max_tries 2 and 3 at the edge (a new try keeps no last result of the old one); 7 a send held past send_timeout_ms is timed_out/unknown, never resent on its try; 8 a refused secret is due after delay/4 with rearm and sent on the same try, and retries_exhausted at max_attempts; 9 a 400 is permanent and a 302 is not followed; 10 enqueue/3 and register/3 idempotency, conflict, 65,536/65,537-byte payloads, zero deliveries and bounds; 11 a repeated record/3 counts once and writes one dead letter, a failed put leaves pending until file_dead_letters/3 files it once, stale_try, no_result, stored observation over fallback, an Adapter observation write in flight before the fallback's insert wins over it, deadline_before_dispatch, deadline_expired and the not_sent fallback; 12 verify/1 passes, claim_due/3, record/3 and status/3 of one tenant neither see nor change another tenant's rows (the Piece's queries also filter the tenant, so row security itself is exercised by verify/1 and by direct T2 inserts failing with 42501), in_transaction before any query and isolation under repeatable read; 13 no payload or secret in errors or inspect. Negative controls, each a temporary edit reverted: a new try for a non-dedup endpoint fails case 5, skipping the send-time egress check fails case 2, claiming without the lease fails case 4, dead-lettering without the pending mark fails case 11. Finite scenarios, not proofs.

PostgreSQL 19 SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING waiting for a concurrent inserter, row locks, COLLATE "C" byte order, row-level security and transaction_isolation are upstream server contracts reached through Postgrex 0.22.4.
Ecto SQL 3.14.0 Repo.transact/2, in_transaction?/0, Ecto.Adapters.SQL.query!/4 with log: false, migration execute/1 and the query telemetry event are upstream behavior.

Req 0.7.5 with retry: false and redirect: false makes one request and returns a 3xx without following it; Req.merge/2 replaces connect_options as a whole; the :plug option runs a function plug in process with no socket; a TransportError reason :timeout is a receive timeout.
The tests' receiver is a Plug.Conn function plug run by Req.Test; Req.Test.raw_body/1 returns the request body bytes.
Pinned Jason encodes an ordered object without white space for the canonical payload, argument and delivery ID bytes.
The tests attach to the Repos' query events to hold one claim inside its transaction and to observe that no query runs inside a caller's transaction.
Elixir String.valid?/1, the utf8 binary pattern, Regex anchors, Base.decode64/2 and Task.yield/2 with Task.shutdown/2 for the send timeout.
OTP 29.1.2 :crypto.mac/4 HMAC-SHA-256, :crypto.hash/2 SHA-256, :crypto.hash_equals/2, :rand.uniform/1 and process semantics.

The consumer runs the migrations as the table owner, connects the application as a non-owner, non-bypass role with the README grants, runs transactions at read committed, calls verify/1 at startup, supplies a trusted clock, a transport Need that connects only to the given addresses and bounds its connection pools, a tenant policy and Secrets context, keeps one live effect-intent owner per key and reads its status for the record/3 fallback, and does not record the Repo's query telemetry parameters.

telemetry.contract: The Piece emits no events and no logs; its queries pass log: false, and the consumer Repo's query telemetry is unchanged (a limit: it receives the parameters).

config.contract: The binding from new/1 is construction-time Config with fixed bounds: repo, prefix, policy, resolver, transport and secrets Needs, clock, a retry policy (max_attempts at most 256, max_backoff_ms at most 2^53-1), max_tries 1..16, send_timeout_ms 1..60,000, try_deadline_ms 1,000..86,400,000, dead-letter store and effect binding; new/1 refuses anything else as invalid. No ambient settings and no hot change: a changed setting is a new binding, applied to later calls.

control.contract: No process or lifecycle of its own; dispatch and rearm are the delivery/effect-intent owner's Control, and the host owns the worker, the Repo, the migrations and the roles.
